cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Colossae (Colossians 1:1-2). He just said the Father brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son (Colossians 1:13). Now he tells who that Son is, and friend, he starts BIG: "The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation."
Then Paul goes on: in Him all things were created, right down to thrones, dominions, rulers and authorities.

cards.question: Paul says all things were created in the Son. Which of these does he include?
Paul names thrones, dominions, rulers and authorities. True or false: Paul says powers like these were made apart from the Son.

cards.text: All things were created through Him and for Him. And Paul says the Son is before all things: before the first oven ever warmed up, before the first batch, He was already there.

cards.question: Paul says the Son is before all things. True or false: Paul also says all things hold together in Him.

cards.text: Now Paul turns to the church and pictures it as a body, with the Son as its head. He's also the beginning, the firstborn from among the dead.

cards.question: Paul says the Son is the beginning and the firstborn from among the dead. What's it all for?

answers.text: So He has first place in all things
So the church grows in number
So the prophets are proven true

cards.text: Then Paul tells what pleased God about the Son, and it has to do with God's fullness and where it dwells. Remember, this is the Son who's the image of the invisible God.

cards.question: Paul says something pleased God about the Son. True or false: God was pleased to have only part of His fullness dwell in Him.

cards.text: And God was pleased, through the Son, to reconcile all things to Himself, things on earth and things in heaven. Not some things, friend. ALL things.

cards.question: God reconciles all things to Himself through the Son. How is that peace made?

answers.text: Through the blood of His cross
Through the law given at Sinai

cards.text: Now Paul makes it personal. He reminds the Colossians how things used to stand between them and God.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Colossians how things used to be. True or false: he says they were once close to God and at peace with Him.

cards.text: Paul says they were alienated from God and hostile in their minds, engaging in evil deeds. But now they've been reconciled by Christ's physical body through death.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the Colossians were reconciled to be presented holy, unblemished and blameless in His presence.

cards.text: Then Paul adds an if: if indeed they continue in their faith, established and firm. Not "I'm getting up early tomorrow" firm, the kind the snooze button beats EVERY morning.

cards.question: Paul's if is that the Colossians continue in their faith, established and firm, and not moved from something. What is it?

answers.text: The hope of the gospel they heard
The law handed down by Moses

cards.question: Paul says this gospel has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven. What does he say he has become?
